title: The Rivergate of the Upper Fly River
premise: Yara Vasquez runs a salvage crew along the abandoned rail spurs of the Upper Fly River basin, keeping ahead of debts and the memories of a survey expedition that went wrong twelve years ago. When her old rival Dario Kessler hires her crew to reopen the Rivergate—a flooded tunnel complex her father died sealing—she accepts because refusing would expose how much she already knows about what lies inside. As the monsoon closes in, the crew uncovers the expedition's true cargo: a ledger of bribes proving the railway was built to move stolen heritage artifacts, implicating the families who now fund Kessler's empire. Yara must choose between burying the truth again and detonating the Rivergate to keep it from Kessler, and the book ends with her flooding the tunnel on her own terms, delivering the ledger to the river communities, and finally letting her crew stop moving.
about_author: Ines Vasquez is a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping decommissioned rail lines across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about the people who keep infrastructure alive long after the world forgets it exists.

chapters.title: Dead Rails, Live Debts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Her crew rerails a washed-out spur for a mining outfit, paid late and under threat. Establishes the crew's rhythm of constant motion and Yara's rule: never take a contract twice, never stay a season. Beat: weary competence masking fear of stillness.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Yara studies her father's hand-drawn survey of the Rivergate spur, the one line marked in red ink with a single word: sealed. Her second-in-command, Tomas, asks why she keeps a map she never uses. Beat: the past pressing through routine.

chapters.title: An Offer from Kessler
chapters.summary: Dario Kessler arrives at camp with contracts, helicopters, and the one job sworn off: reopen the Rivergate before monsoon. He knows her father's name, her debts, her crew's payroll. Yara refuses. Beat: dread dressed as defiance.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: Kessler buys the mining company's debts, leaving Yara's crew unpaid and stranded. Crew members begin defecting to his expedition. Yara realizes refusal means losing everyone anyway. Beat: the trap closing.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Yara negotiates: she leads, she picks the crew, and no one enters the lower gallery. Kessler agrees too easily. POV shifts briefly to Kessler, who notes she still flinches at the word 'gallery.' Beat: a bargain with hidden teeth.

chapters.title: The Crew Assembles
chapters.summary: Yara recruits: explosives expert Nia, hydrologist Okonkwo, and her estranged cousin Bea, a diver who hasn't spoken to her since the funeral. Old wounds surface in logistics talk. Beat: family as both liability and lifeline.

chapters.title: Up the Fly
chapters.summary: The expedition travels by barge through river communities that go quiet at Kessler's name. An elder gives Yara a carved token and says her father promised the river would be returned. Beat: unease among strangers who seem to know more.

chapters.title: First Sight of the Gate
chapters.summary: The crew reaches the portal: a concrete face in the gorge, half-drowned, with blast damage from twelve years ago. Yara recognizes her own father's demolition patterns. Beat: grief made architectural.

chapters.title: The Sworn-Off Job
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Yara's POV. The original survey expedition: her father's discovery in the lower gallery, the argument, the explosion, the sealed tunnel. She was seventeen and signed the report. Beat: guilt revealed.

chapters.title: Pumping the Dark
chapters.summary: Dewatering begins. Okonkwo warns the water table is wrong—the tunnel isn't leaking, something upstream is holding water back. Nia finds modern blasting caps already inside. Beat: they are not the first to return.

chapters.title: The Watcher on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Tomas spots figures observing camp at night. Bea tracks them and finds a river-community scout, who warns: 'The families sent Kessler. The families sent your father. Ask him what he found.' Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: The Upper Gallery Opens
chapters.summary: The crew breaks through into the upper gallery: intact track, sealed crates, and survey brass tags stamped with her father's initials. Yara pockets one. Beat: wonder curdling into recognition.

chapters.title: Crates Without Manifests
chapters.summary: Nia opens a crate against orders: carved panels, ceremonial objects, museum-grade packing from a shipping firm owned by Kessler's backers. Yara orders it resealed. Beat: the job's true shape emerges.

chapters.title: Kessler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara confronts Kessler; he admits the artifacts but frames recovery as rescue from looters. He offers her a partnership and her father's original survey journal, held as leverage. Beat: corruption offering itself as salvation.

chapters.title: The Journal
chapters.summary: Reading her father's journal, Yara learns he found not just artifacts but a ledger documenting the bribes—the same families now funding Kessler. His 'accident' was no accident. Beat: inheritance revealed as a weapon.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warnings
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's models move the monsoon landfall up by nine days. Kessler orders double shifts and cuts the safety margins Yara demanded. Bea sides with Kessler's schedule. Beat: time and trust both eroding.

chapters.title: The Lower Gallery Lock
chapters.summary: Kessler's men breach the door Yara's father built. Yara finds her father's final message scratched inside: 'Flood it. Tell no one. The river keeps what it keeps.' Beat: a father's last order versus a daughter's curiosity.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, lower gallery. She sees the full cache: not just stolen objects but the expedition's evidence room, preserved by the flood her father caused. She photographs the ledger pages and tells no one. Beat: the secret becomes hers.

chapters.title: Bea's Dive
chapters.summary: Bea's POV. A sump dive to map the flood channel goes wrong; Bea nearly drowns and is saved by Yara breaking her own safety protocol. In the aftermath, Bea admits she took Kessler's side to force Yara to talk about the past. Beat: rupture and reconciliation.

chapters.title: The First Theft
chapters.summary: Kessler's crew quietly loads artifacts onto the barge at night. Nia, uneasy, tells Yara. Yara lets it happen to keep her cover, hating herself. Beat: complicity's cost.

chapters.title: The Elder's Token
chapters.summary: The river communities arrive at camp, led by the elder. They don't want the artifacts for museums; they want them home, and they want the ledger. Yara shows them nothing but gives them the carved token back. Beat: divided loyalties made flesh.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone floods the pump line. Kessler accuses the river people; Yara suspects Kessler staged it to justify arming his crew. Tomas is hurt in the resulting scuffle. Beat: the expedition turns on itself.

chapters.title: Nia's Choice
chapters.summary: Nia's POV. Ordered to prepare demolition charges for 'stabilization,' she realizes Kessler plans to collapse the lower gallery—destroying the ledger evidence—once the artifacts are out. Beat: the crew's moral fault lines harden.

chapters.title: The Confession at the Portal
chapters.summary: Yara tells Bea the truth about the original expedition: she signed the closure report her father's killers dictated, believing she was protecting the crew. Bea forgives her, then asks the harder question: what will she sign this time? Beat: absolution with a challenge.

chapters.title: Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: The storm hits early. The river rises six feet in a night; the barge with the first artifact shipment is stranded mid-channel. Kessler orders the crew to save the cargo before the people. Beat: values exposed under pressure.

chapters.title: Saving the Barge
chapters.summary: Yara leads a night rescue of Kessler's stranded workers, using the dead rails as a guide line through the flood. Several of Kessler's men defect to her side afterward. Beat: leadership as moral argument.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Pages
chapters.summary: Yara secretly passes photographed ledger pages to the elder's people via the scout. Kessler's surveillance catches the exchange. He confronts Yara privately: he's known about her father's journal since he hired her. Beat: the mask drops.

chapters.title: Kessler's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Kessler reveals he has Bea's dive records falsified to show negligence—if Yara interferes, Bea loses her certification and the crew faces criminal charges. He gives her until the water recedes to hand over the journal. Beat: power's purest form: leverage over love.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, alone with the journal and her father's scratched message. She drafts two plans: comply and vanish, or flood the gallery and destroy her own credibility. Tomas, unasked, stands watch outside her tent. Beat: the darkest hour.

chapters.title: The Crew Decides
chapters.summary: Yara tells the crew everything. Nia offers her charges; Okonkwo maps the flood channel; Bea volunteers for the dive that will open the sluice. No one votes to comply. Beat: solidarity forged in truth.

chapters.title: The Counterfeit Shipment
chapters.summary: The crew loads the remaining crates—but with replicas Nia and the river people built from plaster and river clay, buying time while the real objects move upstream to the communities. Beat: cunning as resistance.

chapters.title: The Sluice Dive
chapters.summary: Bea's POV. The dive to open the old sluice gate in rising floodwater, guided by Yara's voice on the line. Bea finds her father's spare tag on the gate mechanism—he built the flood option in. Beat: terror transfigured into inheritance.

chapters.title: Kessler's Last Train
chapters.summary: Kessler, tipped off by a defector's radio, races to move the counterfeit crates and discovers the swap. He takes Yara hostage at the portal, journal in hand, demanding the real ledger location. Beat: confrontation at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Rivergate Floods
chapters.summary: Bea opens the sluice. The lower gallery floods on Yara's father's terms, destroying Kessler's evidence room and nearly taking Yara with it; Tomas pulls her out. Kessler flees upstream with his fakes. Beat: the climax—the past finally sealed properly.

chapters.title: What the Water Took
chapters.summary: Aftermath in the gorge. The crew accounts for everyone; the original artifacts are safe with the river communities; the ledger copies are beyond Kessler's reach. Yara grieves her father a second time, properly this time. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Report
chapters.summary: Yara files the official report: structural failure, monsoon flooding, no recoverable cargo. The same lie she signed at seventeen—but this time it's hers, chosen, and it protects people instead of predators. Beat: reclaiming the signature.

chapters.title: Kessler's Reckoning
chapters.summary: News arrives that the ledger copies reached journalists and prosecutors; Kessler's backers are abandoning him. He sends Yara one message: 'Your father would be proud.' She doesn't answer. Beat: justice as aftermath, not spectacle.

chapters.title: The River Returned
chapters.summary: The communities hold a ceremony reopening the river channel; the artifacts come home to the villages, not the museums. The elder tells Yara her father's promise is kept. Beat: inheritance honored.

chapters.title: The Crew That Stopped
chapters.summary: The crew takes a contract near the rivergate basin—a permanent maintenance job, the first time any of them has agreed to stay a season. Bea and Yara plan a survey of the living lines, the ones still running. Beat: stillness chosen, not feared.

chapters.title: The Open Line
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV. She revises her father's map: the red line through the Rivergate now marked not 'sealed' but 'returned.' She mails a copy to no one, keeps it for herself, and watches the first train in twelve years cross the upper spur. Beat: peace earned; the journey home complete.
